Inspect a finite set of prespecified imputation assumptions

Source: R/analysis.R
catmech_sensitivity.Rd

Inspired by assumption-path audits: keep failed and unresolved scenarios visible, and do not select the most favorable result. The interval envelope is descriptive; it is not a confidence interval over arbitrary misspecification. It covers only the supplied finite set and inherits each member's limitations.

Usage

catmech_sensitivity(
  results,
  formula = NULL,
  term,
  reference = 0,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  expected_scenarios = NULL,
  cluster = NULL,
  cluster_variance = c("cv3", "cr1s"),
  method = c("pool_lm", "pool_glm", "pool_coxph", "marginal_summary", "joint_summary"),
  family = stats::binomial()
)

Arguments

results

A uniquely named list of catmech_result objects or error conditions captured with tryCatch(..., error = identity). Supply every prespecified scenario, including failures.

formula

A prespecified linear analysis formula, identical across scenarios. When `method = "marginal_summary"`, `formula` is optional and defaults to the population regression of the true measurement on the continuous predictors; it can also specify a custom response and covariate subset (e.g. `outcome ~ recorded + x`). When `method = "joint_summary"`, `formula` is not used.

term

Name of the coefficient to compare.

reference

Reference value, usually zero, for interval-direction reporting.

conf_level

Conditional confidence level passed to [catmech_pool_lm()] or [catmech_marginal_summary()] / [catmech_joint_summary()].

expected_scenarios

Optional character vector naming the complete prespecified set. Omitted members are recorded as failures; unplanned extras are rejected. Without this argument only supplied scenarios can be checked.

cluster, cluster_variance

Passed to [catmech_pool_lm()], so that fits made with and without `catmech_reference(cluster = )` can be compared under the same variance. Without `cluster`, a fit with its own cluster column uses a cluster-robust variance and a fit without one a model-based variance, and their widths are not comparable.

method

Estimation method: `"pool_lm"` (default) for multiple-imputation pooling of linear fits, `"pool_glm"` for generalized linear model pooling, `"pool_coxph"` for Cox proportional hazards model pooling via [catmech_pool_coxph()], `"marginal_summary"` for population marginal inference from [catmech_marginal_summary()], or `"joint_summary"` for fixed-effect summaries from [catmech_joint_summary()].

family

Error distribution and link function for `method = "pool_glm"`. Defaults to `stats::binomial()`.

Value

A list with table, status, complete, successful_envelope and interpretation. An incomplete scenario set always has an unresolved status.

Examples

set.seed(123)
df <- data.frame(
  lab = stats::rnorm(30, 10, 2),
  age = stats::rnorm(30, 50, 10),
  y = stats::rnorm(30, 5, 1)
)
df$ref <- df$lab
df$ref[11:30] <- NA
res1 <- catmech_reference(df, value = "lab", reference = "ref",
                          predictors = "age", m = 2, seed = 1)
res2 <- catmech_reference(df, value = "lab", reference = "ref",
                          predictors = "age", use_recorded = TRUE, m = 2, seed = 2)
#> Warning: All 10 audited rows agree with their recorded values, so 20 unaudited recorded values were kept with no imputation uncertainty. An audit of this size cannot rule out an error rate of about 30.0%, and intervals here treat those records as correct.
sens <- catmech_sensitivity(
  list(standard = res1, recorded = res2),
  formula = y ~ lab + age, term = "lab"
)
#> Warning: Every audited row agreed, so unaudited recorded values were kept, and these intervals treat them as correct.
print(sens)
#> -- Catmech Sensitivity Analysis --
#> Status:              unresolved_in_all_scenarios (complete: TRUE)
#> Successful envelope: [-0.114, 0.5184]
#> Scenarios:           2 evaluated
#> 
#>  scenario status estimate std.error   lower  upper          direction
#>  standard     ok   0.2246    0.1256 -0.0692 0.5184 includes_reference
#>  recorded     ok   0.0564    0.0828 -0.1140 0.2268 includes_reference
